impact.title: Our Vision
impact.subtitle: What we want to build for Africa and its people
impact.manifestoText: Millions of Africans lack access to formal employment, recognized qualifications, or professional networks. LIBOSO wants to change that: formalize services, train without requiring degrees, and put women at the heart of Africa's digital revolution.
impact.pillarsSubtitle: Each pillar guides our decisions, our product, and our future impact
impact.pillar1Desc: Transform informal workers into certified service providers with contracts, stable income and social protection.
impact.pillar2Desc: Practical training accessible to everyone — whether you have a diploma or not. What matters is your motivation.
impact.pillar3Desc: Women make up the majority of our agent network. We train them, support them, and give them the tools to succeed.
impact.pillar4Desc: Accessible services with local payments: M-Pesa, Airtel Money, bank cards — no price or technology barriers.
impact.pillar5Desc: Become one of Africa's most-used service platforms, starting with DRC, Rwanda and Kenya.
impact.womenText: On a continent where women are the first to suffer from unemployment and economic exclusion, LIBOSO puts women at the center of its model.
impact.womenPoint1: Priority access to free professional training
impact.womenPoint2: Personalized support to become a certified agent
impact.womenPoint3: Goal: 50%+ women in our agent network
impact.womenStat1: Target share of women agents in the network
impact.womenStat2: Cost to enroll in our training programs
impact.womenStat3: Recognized certification upon completion of each program
impact.trainingSubtitle: No degree required. Just your motivation and time.
impact.training1Desc: Short modules (1 to 4 weeks) to quickly enter the job market.
impact.training2Desc: Each learner is accompanied by an experienced agent in the field.
impact.training3Desc: From basic agent to supervisor, then trainer — a real career path.
impact.training4Desc: Our goal: 100% of graduates integrated into our network or partner companies.
impact.leaderTitle: Becoming a Digital Leader in Africa
impact.leaderText: LIBOSO is not just an app. It is infrastructure for African urban services — scalable, bilingual, and cross-border.
impact.digital1Desc: Booking, payment, tracking — all from your phone, no travel required.
impact.digital2Desc: Integration of M-Pesa, Airtel Money, Orange Money, bank cards and low-cost payments.
impact.oddSubtitle: Our vision directly aligns with the Sustainable Development Goals
impact.ctaText: Whether you are a client, agent, investor or partner — there is a place for you in this African revolution.

pages.problemSubtitle: In the Democratic Republic of Congo, the informal economy dominates most urban service activities: cleaning, street commerce, small repair services, car washing, and domestic services.
pages.problemClickHint: Click each red point to read details.

problemTimeline.step1Desc:
● About 80% of workers in DRC operate in the informal sector.
● Nearly 2.9 million informal businesses exist in urban areas.
● Cleaning, street commerce, and related services represent around 11.2% of informal activities.
problemTimeline.step2Desc:
● Urban population growth: 4.5% to 4.6% per year.
● Urban population: over 50 million inhabitants.
problemTimeline.step3Desc:
Rapid urbanization increases demand for:
● Car washing
● Home and office cleaning
● Gardening
● Waste management
● Digital booking services
problemTimeline.step4Desc:
The cleaning and urban services market in DRC is large and growing because:
● Cities are developing quickly
● Most services remain informal
● There is a shortage of reliable, digitized providers

Sources:
● African Development Bank report
● UN-Habitat urbanization data
● Macrotrends urban population data
